$comment: Demiton SM038: the events that start an obligation's clock. Each is a fact already held in a register; this catalogue says which facts count as which event, which field dates them, and whose clock they start. Not a register of events. An obligation names one as its `trigger`. `subject`: project (one clock per job), asset or worker (one per spine entity), reference (one per triggering record, matched by `reference_field` on the trigger and `proof_reference_fields` on the proof). `match`: field values a trigger record must have. `requires_item`: the record must have an entry in that array field (matching `match` within the entry, if given). Fields are checked against contracts/ by scripts/validate.py.

claim_lodged.description: A payment claim was lodged (given) under the contract or a security of payment Act.
claim_lodged.subject: reference

machine_started.description: A machine's ignition was switched on. REVIEW: the value `ignition` is this draft's reading of the contract's discriminator; the compliance gate today reads the raw telematics field `action == "ON"`, so confirm what the Navman projection writes before release.
machine_started.subject: asset

incident_recorded.description: A safety incident was recorded (the event a regulator notice runs from).
incident_recorded.subject: reference

delay_recorded.description: A site diary recorded a delay: any entry in its `delays` list, of any kind.
delay_recorded.subject: project

latent_condition_reported.description: A site diary recorded a delay of kind `latent_condition` (site_diary 1.1.0). A diary whose source fills no `kind` starts no latent-condition clock.
latent_condition_reported.subject: project
